d.d: A domestic servant, generally male, who would attend upon (usually several) students, brushing their clothes, carrying parcels, waiting at parties and other tasks; generally equivalent to a scout in the historical sense at Oxford University or a skip at Trinity College, Dublin.
The room in which such college servants work.
A mineral consisting of hydrated calcium sulphate. When calcinated, it forms plaster of Paris.
An itinerant person or any person, not necessarily Romani; a tinker, a traveller or a carny.
A member of a Broadway musical chorus line.
A member of other nomadic peoples, not only of the Romani people; a traveller. Alternative spelling of gypsy.
To roam around the country like a gypsy.
To perform the gypsy step in contra dancing.
